subject: radiology
title: Radiation Shielding and Protection in Pregnancy: AERB Regulations

steps.title: Lead Apron Attenuation Physics
steps.tx: **Lead apron attenuation** shields clinical personnel against scattered X-ray radiation. Standard protective aprons provide 0.25 to 0.5 millimetres of lead equivalence, manufactured from lead-impregnated vinyl or rubber polymers. A 0.5-millimetre lead equivalent apron attenuates approximately 90 to 95 percent of scattered radiation generated at diagnostic tube potentials between 70 and 100 kilovolts.

steps.tx: Protective clothing only works when every exposed worker in the fluoroscopy room wears the full set together. The photograph checks a wraparound apron of stated lead equivalence, a snug **thyroid collar** protecting the gland in the scatter field, and lead acrylic glasses for the lens. Fit matters over a long list: gaps at the neck or axilla leave tissue exposed despite an apron hanging nearby on the rack.
steps.say: Full protection means a fitted lead apron, thyroid collar and lead glasses worn together in the scatter field. Gaps at the neck or axilla leave tissue exposed.

steps.title: Thyroid and Eye Protective Barriers
steps.tx: **Thyroid shield protection** incorporates a separate collar providing 0.5 millimetres of lead equivalence fastened securely around the anterior neck. Because the thyroid gland has a high tissue weighting factor of 0.04 and vulnerability to radiation-induced carcinoma, collar shielding reduces scatter dose by over 80 percent. Lead acrylic eyewear with 0.75-millimetre equivalence protects against cataractogenesis.

steps.title: Apron Handling and Structural Integrity
steps.tx: **Lead apron maintenance** mandates hanging garments on dedicated heavy-duty hangers or storing them flat on flat examination surfaces. Folding, creasing, or dropping lead aprons causes internal fractures and tearing of the brittle lead-rubber shielding layer. Facilities must perform annual fluoroscopic or radiographic screening to inspect aprons for occult cracks and tear defects.

steps.title: Pre-implantation All-or-None Response
steps.tx: **Pre-implantation radiation response** governs the initial two weeks following conception, corresponding to menstrual weeks 3 and 4. During this blastocyst cleavage phase, ionizing radiation operates under an all-or-none biological rule: embryonic damage either proves lethal, resulting in failure of implantation or occult spontaneous resorption, or surviving totipotent cells completely repair the damage without congenital malformations.

left.title: Lethal Blastocyst Insult
points: High-dose radiation kills critical fraction of blastomeres

right.title: Complete Totipotent Recovery
points: Surviving totipotent stem cells compensate for loss

steps.tx: One dose does not mean one injury, because the week decides the harm. In the first fortnight after conception the embryo is lost or it is spared, which is the all-or-none window already described for implantation. During organ formation the risk is malformation. From about eight to fifteen weeks the brain is the sensitive organ, and a high fetal dose is linked with **microcephaly** and later intellectual disability. Shielding and a justified radiograph are judged against that timeline, not against a single threshold for the whole of pregnancy.
steps.say: Before implantation radiation tends to cause loss of the embryo or no effect. In organogenesis the risk is malformation. From eight to fifteen weeks a high dose is linked with microcephaly. The week sets the injury.

steps.title: Organogenesis Teratogenic Risks
steps.tx: **Organogenesis teratogenic risk** spans post-conception weeks 3 through 8, corresponding to gestational weeks 5 through 10. Rapid cellular differentiation renders organ systems susceptible to structural malformations. The deterministic threshold for gross structural anomalies, including skeletal dysplasias, cleft palate, and cardiac defects, is roughly 100 to 200 milligrays, an exposure never reached during routine diagnostic imaging.

steps.title: Neurogenesis and Intellectual Impairment
steps.tx: **Neurogenesis intellectual impairment** peaks during post-conception weeks 8 through 15, when neuronal stem cells proliferate and migrate to form the cerebral cortex. Radiation exposure exceeding 100 milligrays causes dose-dependent microcephaly and severe intellectual disability, with an estimated loss of 25 to 30 IQ points per gray. Medical termination of pregnancy is never justified below 100 milligrays.

steps.title: Law of Bergonie and Tribondeau
steps.tx: **Bergonie and Tribondeau law** established in 1906 states that the radiosensitivity of biological tissue is directly proportional to its mitotic rate and inversely proportional to its degree of differentiation. Consequently, erythroblasts, spermatogonia, and intestinal crypt cells are exquisitely radiosensitive. The notable exception is the mature circulating lymphocyte, which, despite non-dividing status, undergoes rapid apoptosis following radiation.

steps.title: AERB Regulations and Facility Shielding
steps.tx: **Atomic Energy Regulatory Board** statutory mandates enforce diagnostic radiation safety across India under the Atomic Energy Act. Installations must obtain site clearance, layout approval, and operating licensing through the e-LORA digital portal. Structural regulations require diagnostic X-ray room walls to provide lead shielding equivalent to at least 2 millimetres of lead or 23 centimetres of solid red brick.
